_about: Layer 3 (EXPLAIN) mechanism assessments, one record per mechanism, in the shape of the team's layer contracts (section 4, Output: Evidence Ledger). Status values per expected observation: consistent | inconsistent | unclear | not_tested. Numbers come from Layer 1/2 evidence (docs/research/evidence_ledger.md, E-IDs); this file only interprets them. Draft written with AI assistance (Claude Code) for review by the science lead: researcher_interpretation and confidence must be confirmed by a team member. References are literature IDs that are still TO-VERIFY (not yet read).
region: Sahel box 10-20N, 18W-20E, with provisional W/C/E sub-regions (D-003b)
detected_trend_summary: Season totals: wetting tendency (+3.3 %/decade, p = 0.15), stronger in the east (+8.7 %, p = 0.055, partly driven by 2024). Longest dry spell: shortening, robust in the east (-9.6 %/decade, p = 0.001). Extremes: inconclusive (2014 satellite-era change in the daily tail).

mechanisms.name: West African Monsoon circulation (dynamic moisture supply)
mechanisms.scientific_description: A stronger or more northward-reaching monsoon brings more moist air from the Gulf of Guinea, increases low-level moisture convergence and large-scale rising motion, and so produces more rain days and shorter dry spells, independently of local warming.

expected_observations.expectation: Stronger southerly monsoon inflow at 850 hPa
expected_observations.observed: V850 +0.15 m/s per decade, p < 0.001 (all sub-regions)

expected_observations.expectation: Stronger low-level westerlies (monsoon flow)
expected_observations.observed: U850 no significant trend (box p = 0.28; east p = 0.20); strongly positive only in 2024 (+3.1 sigma)

expected_observations.expectation: More moisture convergence
expected_observations.observed: +0.35 mm/day per decade, p = 0.002; detrended rho with rainfall 0.73

expected_observations.expectation: More large-scale rising motion
expected_observations.observed: rising motion at 500 hPa up, p = 0.02; rho with rainfall 0.72

expected_observations.expectation: Rain days up and dry spells shorter
expected_observations.observed: Dry spells shorter in the east (robust, p <= 0.004 in every test); wet days +1.5 %/decade, not significant

expected_observations.expectation: Moistening not explained by local warming
expected_observations.observed: JJAS T2M flat (box) or cooling (east, -0.29 C/decade); water vapour vs T2M -4.6 %/K

alternative_explanations: Remote ocean forcing (Atlantic Multidecadal Variability, north-east Atlantic SST) driving the monsoon change: an upstream cause rather than a competitor (L-23; research_references 2026 #2)
Changes in aerosol forcing, e.g. Asian sulfate emissions (L-22)
Natural decadal variability over a short (28-year) record
Reanalysis artefact: MERRA-2 circulation trends can follow changes in assimilated observations
mechanisms.researcher_interpretation: DRAFT for review: the strongest-supported mechanism. Every circulation indicator except the zonal wind moves in the expected direction and tracks rainfall year to year. It explains why dry spells shorten without local warming.
limitations: Box-mean winds mix monsoon (south) and Saharan (north) regimes
No second reanalysis or observed humidity product yet

mechanisms.name: Atmospheric moisture availability (thermodynamic, Clausius-Clapeyron)
mechanisms.scientific_description: Warmer air can hold about 7 % more water vapour per kelvin. If local warming drives the moistening, water vapour should rise with temperature and heavy-rain intensity should rise faster than totals.

expected_observations.expectation: Column water vapour increases
expected_observations.observed: +1.67 kg/m2 per decade (+4.1 %/decade), p = 0.001

expected_observations.expectation: Local near-surface warming in the rainy season
expected_observations.observed: No warming (box -0.13 C/decade, p = 0.21; east -0.29, p = 0.02)

expected_observations.expectation: Water vapour scales with temperature at about +7 %/K
expected_observations.observed: -4.6 %/K year to year (wetter years are cooler)

expected_observations.expectation: Heavy-rain indices track moisture
expected_observations.observed: Detrended rho of Rx1day 0.70, R95p 0.78 with water vapour (p < 0.001)

expected_observations.expectation: Heavy-rain intensity increases over time
expected_observations.observed: Rx1day no trend (p = 0.42); SDII +2.3 %/decade but mostly a step at 2014

alternative_explanations: Moisture rise supplied by circulation (M-01) rather than local temperature
Global/ocean warming raising moisture upstream, which local land temperature cannot show
mechanisms.researcher_interpretation: DRAFT for review: the moisture increase is real in MERRA-2, but local temperature does not explain it. The thermodynamic pathway may act through ocean or global warming upstream, which we have not tested. Extremes respond to moisture year to year, so the missing extreme-rain trend is more likely a data problem (2014 tail) than an absence of effect.
limitations: Local T2M is cooled by rain and cloud, so it is a weak test
A proper scaling test uses event-scale extremes vs temperature or dew point

mechanisms.name: Organized convection (mesoscale convective systems)
mechanisms.scientific_description: Most Sahel rain falls from organized storm systems. More moisture and instability, and stronger wind shear, make them rain harder; extremes can rise even when storm numbers stay stable.

expected_observations.expectation: Stronger mid-level rising motion
Extreme rain tracks ascent year to year
expected_observations.observed: Detrended rho: Rx1day 0.73, R95p 0.76 with ascent

expected_observations.expectation: Rain per event and extremes increase
expected_observations.observed: Rx1day no trend; SDII up but possibly a satellite-era artefact

expected_observations.expectation: Deep convective cores with strong Doppler updrafts in recent storms
expected_observations.observed: EarthCARE CPR, 3 storms (W/C/E): radar echo tops 15.5-17.2 km (95th pct of rainy profiles), up to 18 km (tropopause); air-motion updrafts up to 6-9 m/s at 4-10 km; heavy rain below the 4.7 km melting level. Snapshots of present-day storms, not a trend

expected_observations.expectation: Stronger wind shear (L-20, L-21)
expected_observations.observed: Shear not yet computed (needs 600-925 hPa winds, M2IMNPASM)

alternative_explanations: Changes in storm frequency rather than intensity
Satellite-era changes in how IMERG resolves convective peaks (E-006)
mechanisms.researcher_interpretation: DRAFT for review: EarthCARE shows that today's Sahel rain comes from deep organized systems reaching the tropopause with strong updrafts, which is the storm type through which more moisture would produce heavier rain. Whether these storms have become more intense over time cannot be shown by EarthCARE (2024 onwards); that test still depends on the daily rain-gauge check of extremes.
limitations: AC-TC labels thin layers near the tropopause as dust: treated as an artefact (only dust below 8 km used)
EarthCARE covers 2024-2025 only: process illustration, never a trend
Needs daily rain-gauge check of extremes

mechanisms.name: Dust and aerosol interactions
mechanisms.scientific_description: Saharan dust absorbs and scatters sunlight and can change cloud formation, which may suppress or shift rainfall. Its effect depends on altitude, particle type and cloud regime.

expected_observations.expectation: Dust load changes over time
expected_observations.observed: Dust optical depth -0.03 per decade (-8 %/decade), p < 0.001

expected_observations.expectation: Dustier seasons are drier (same season)
expected_observations.observed: Detrended rho with JJAS rainfall -0.12, p = 0.54

expected_observations.expectation: Dust before the season (MAM) precedes drier JJAS
expected_observations.observed: Detrended rho -0.07, p = 0.72

expected_observations.expectation: Dust layer sits at or above cloud level in storms
expected_observations.observed: EarthCARE AC-TC: dust (Saharan Air Layer) at 1-6 km, median 3.0-3.5 km; dry June case: dust over 96 % of the box. In storm cases dust lies BESIDE the storms (dust and rain in the same profile < 1 %). The lidar is blocked under thick storm cloud, so dust inside storms cannot be seen

expected_observations.expectation: Extreme dry vs wet years differ in dust

alternative_explanations: Reverse causality: wetter, greener seasons emit less dust
Assimilation artefact in MERRA-2 aerosols (MODIS AOD assimilated; 2025 anomaly -3 sigma)
Remote aerosol forcing (Asian sulfate, L-22) acting through circulation
mechanisms.researcher_interpretation: DRAFT for review: the dust decline is a trend in the reanalysis, but it does not track rainfall from year to year. At most a secondary player, and possibly a consequence of wetter conditions. EarthCARE confirms a deep Saharan dust layer (1-6 km) next to and north of the storms, but cannot see inside them, so the dust-storm interaction itself stays untested.
limitations: AC-TC labels thin layers near the tropopause as dust: treated as an artefact (only dust below 8 km used)
Column AOD says nothing about dust altitude
Not yet checked against MODIS AOD directly

mechanisms.name: Soil moisture and surface energy balance
mechanisms.scientific_description: Wet soils evaporate more and stay cooler, which can feed moisture back to the atmosphere and change where new storms form; soil-moisture contrasts can strengthen storm systems through wind shear.

expected_observations.expectation: Cooler surface in wetter seasons/regions
expected_observations.observed: Wetter years cooler (rho -0.53); east cooling -0.29 C/decade

expected_observations.expectation: Shorter dry spells where soils stay moist
expected_observations.observed: East dry spells shorter (robust); soil moisture itself not yet tested

expected_observations.expectation: Soil moisture increases in the rainy season
expected_observations.observed: Not fetched (MERRA-2 M2TMNXLND GWETTOP or ESA CCI)

expected_observations.expectation: Greener vegetation (NDVI add-on, D-011)
expected_observations.observed: Not fetched

alternative_explanations: Surface cooling from clouds and rain, not soil moisture
mechanisms.researcher_interpretation: DRAFT for review: not assessed yet. The cooling is consistent but has a simpler explanation (cloud and rain). Needs soil-moisture and NDVI data.
limitations: No soil-moisture or vegetation data in the analysis yet
